bull_thesis: At $77.25 the market is paying roughly 6.7 times trailing free cash flow ($550 million over the last twelve months) for two genuinely global brands, Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, at what looks like a trough in reported earnings. The audited fiscal-2026 net income of $25 million (earnings per share of $0.53, down 95%) is an artifact of tariffs, restructuring and one-time charges layered onto an 8.8% underlying operating margin -- and the most recent quarter's earnings were already up more than 300% year on year as those charges roll off. Management has earned the benefit of the doubt on execution: guidance was beaten in all seven tracked quarters, the Calvin Klein product-organization mess was fixed exactly on the promised spring-2026 schedule (deliveries on time, going margins on plan, inventory down 5%), and over 200 basis points of cost savings were delivered. The capital-return engine is the heart of the case: $560 million of buybacks retired 15% of the share count in fiscal 2025, at least $300 million more is planned this year, and it is funded from free cash flow, not borrowing -- at this price every year of buyback compounds the per-share value materially. Forward evidence is quietly positive: European fall-2026 wholesale order books are up for a second consecutive season, e-commerce is growing across all regions, and open-market insiders are modest net buyers. The re-rate case needs only a return to normal: if fiscal-2027 shows the recovered gross margin management has already locked in for spring 2026 product, roughly $10 of adjusted earnings power on a shrinking share count makes the current price a single-digit multiple on a global brand house. bear_thesis: This is a flat business in a hostile tape, and the cheapness is thinner than it looks. Revenue has gone nowhere for five years ($9.15 billion in fiscal 2022 to $8.95 billion in fiscal 2026), return on invested capital is 6%, and the latest audited year earned a 0.3% net margin -- low multiples on low returns are not automatically a bargain. The near-term earnings bridge is fragile: the reaffirmed fiscal-2026 earnings guidance only survives because a one-time tariff refund of roughly $100 million lands in the second quarter (worth about 470 basis points of that quarter's gross margin); strip it out and the June guide was a cut. The swing region is Europe, and every driver management named in June -- Middle East wholesale demand, the Turkey knock-on, higher fuel costs keeping consumers out of stores -- has gotten worse since: the Hormuz blockade resumed in July and Brent is near $89, a direct tax on PVH's most profitable region. Tariff risk is not behind them either: the proposed Section 301 architecture would put allied sourcing countries at 10 to 12.5%, with retaliation risk, and PVH itself concedes only 75% mitigation exiting this year. The balance sheet is serviceable but not a cushion (net debt $1.69 billion excluding leases, $3.63 billion including the $1.94 billion of store leases; solvency score in the grey zone at 2.2), the finance chair has been filled by an interim chief financial officer for two-plus quarters, and wholesale partners are described as cautious. interrogator_dossier:
# PVH Corp. (PVH) — Forensic Dossier
*Interrogator review of five consecutive earnings calls (June 2025 through June 2026, fiscal 2025 Q1 through fiscal 2026 Q1) cross-referenced against the screener financials. Price at review: $77.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, July 21, 2026.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has been remarkably consistent for five straight quarters: the "PVH+ plan" — lean into the brand strength of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, concentrate on hero categories (underwear and denim for Calvin, sweaters and outerwear for Tommy), amplify with celebrity-led marketing, and grind out cost savings. What changed across the arc is the *external* frame wrapped around that story:

- **June 2025 (Q1):** the first crack — "an increasingly tough environment," a leg down in North American consumer traffic, China weak, tariffs arriving. Full-year gross margin guidance cut from down ~100 basis points to down ~250, half of the extra pain from promotions.
- **August 2025 (Q2):** stabilization tone — beat on top and bottom line, guidance reaffirmed "despite tariff rates effectively doubling."
- **December 2025 (Q3):** confidence building — outlook narrowed to the high end; the Calvin Klein operational mess (late deliveries, weak going margins from standing up the New York global product organization) declared on track to be fixed for spring 2026. CFO Zac Coughlin's departure announced.
- **April 2026 (Q4/full year):** delivery — beat across revenue, operating profit and earnings per share; returned to revenue growth for the year as promised; a striking $560 million of buybacks retiring 15% of shares outstanding; fiscal 2026 guided flat-to-slightly-up with margins held at 8.8%.
- **June 2026 (Q1 fiscal 2026):** a new external shock — the prolonged Middle East conflict crushes the EMEA outlook (direct Middle East wholesale, Turkey knock-on, higher fuel costs suppressing European store traffic). Full-year revenue guidance cut to flat; earnings guidance held *only* because of a one-time ~$100 million tariff-refund benefit landing in Q2.

Two growth drivers were quietly re-weighted along the way: wholesale (early strength driven by shipment timing and the women's license take-back, now described with "cautious partner positioning") and Europe D2C (two strong quarters in early fiscal 2025, then muted). E-commerce and APAC were promoted from footnotes to lead proof points.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Returned to revenue growth" (fiscal 2025) | Revenue $8.95B vs $8.65B prior year, +3.4% reported | True, but reported growth got a currency assist; constant-currency was roughly flat. Five-year picture is a flat top line: $9.15B (fiscal 2022) to $8.95B (fiscal 2026) |
| "Delivered on all commitments across the P&L" | Guidance beaten 7 of 7 quarters (100% beat rate per the screener) | Corroborated — the beat cadence is real, though the bar is management's own guidance, which is set conservatively |
| Non-GAAP operating margin 8.8%, "11% excluding tariffs" | GAAP net income collapsed to $25M (EPS $0.53, down 95%) in fiscal 2026 | The widest GAAP/non-GAAP gap in the record. Roughly $790M of implied non-GAAP operating profit reconciles down to near-zero GAAP net income — tariffs, restructuring and one-time charges absorb almost everything. The adjusted story is much richer than the audited one |
| Strong cash generation funding buybacks | Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow $550M; $560M repurchased (15% of shares) in fiscal 2025 | Corroborated — buybacks are funded by genuine free cash flow, not leverage. The single strongest fact in the file |
| "Calvin Klein operational challenges fixed for spring 2026" | Q1 fiscal 2026: deliveries on time, going margins on plan, inventory down 5% | Delivered as promised, on the schedule set three quarters earlier — a genuine credibility win |
| Tariff mitigation "75% mitigated exiting this year" | Q3 fiscal 2025 gross margin down 210bp of which 110bp tariffs; Q2 fiscal 2026 to book a ~$100M refund | Mitigation is progressing but the refund is a one-time windfall, not mitigation. Watch whether fiscal 2027 margin holds without it |
| Balance sheet health | Net debt $3.63B including $1.94B of capitalized leases ($1.69B excluding leases) against $550M free cash flow; Altman-Z 2.2 (grey zone, not distress) | Manageable, not fortress. Roughly 3x free cash flow on the ex-lease measure |

The core divergence: management narrates brand momentum and beats; the audited financials show a company earning a 0.3% net margin and a 6% return on invested capital in its most recent fiscal year. The truth sits in between — trough GAAP earnings depressed by tariffs and one-offs, against real and improving cash generation (trailing-twelve-month diluted EPS $3.31, latest quarter up over 300% year on year).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive vocabulary creeping in.** Larsson's register barely moves quarter to quarter — the same "iconic brands, hero categories, full-funnel marketing" liturgy every call, which is itself information: no panic, but also little candor about demand. The tells:

- Q1 2025: "when the external factors get worse, it's time to sharpen our focus" — the pivot to controllables begins.
- Q2–Q4 2025: offense resumes ("beat our guidance on both the top and bottom line," "reaffirming... raising").
- Q1 2026: the "two opposing forces" framing — brand momentum versus the war — is the most defensive construction in the file, and the guidance cut it wraps is real.

Guidance specificity *increased* over time (basis-point-level tariff decompositions, region-by-region margin bridges), which typically signals a management team confident in its internal forecasting. The interim chief financial officer, Melissa Stone, has maintained that grain of disclosure.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High on execution, Medium on outlooks.** Every quarter in the record beat the guidance issued the quarter before, consistent with the screener's 7-for-7 beat rate. Two caveats: (1) there is a visible sandbagging pattern — guidance is set to be beaten, so each beat carries less signal than it appears; (2) the full-year outlook was cut twice in thirteen months on external shocks (promotions/tariffs in mid-2025, the Middle East conflict in mid-2026), so the beats coexist with a shrinking bar. Promises with hard deadlines — the spring 2026 Calvin Klein operational fix, the return to fiscal 2025 revenue growth, the 200-basis-point cost-savings program — were all delivered on schedule.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Gross margin recapture** (Boss, Kernan, Binetti, repeatedly): analysts kept probing when the ~250 basis points of fiscal-2025 margin give-up comes back. Management's answer — sequential improvement, spring 2026 going margins — was delivered, but the recapture is now hostage to tariffs and the promotional environment.
- **Macro versus execution attribution** (Boss, Q1 2025): how much of the weakness is self-inflicted? Management consistently attributes to macro; the Calvin operational mess was the one admitted own-goal.
- **Europe durability** (Roach, twice): what is the medium-term European growth algorithm? Management answers with order books (up low single digits), never with a demand algorithm — and Europe is precisely where the 2026 shock landed. The analysts were pulling on the right thread.
- **Wholesale caution** (Q1 2026): "cautious partner positioning" acknowledged — a soft leading indicator worth respecting.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The GAAP/non-GAAP chasm** — fiscal 2026 GAAP net income of $25M against a narrated 8.8% non-GAAP operating margin. The adjustments are individually defensible (tariffs, restructuring) but the cumulative gap is the largest in the company's recent record.
🔴 **CFO churn** — Coughlin out (announced December 2025), an interim chief financial officer through two earnings cycles and counting, with no permanent appointment as of July 2026.
🔴 **Earnings guidance held together by a one-timer** — the reaffirmed fiscal 2026 earnings guide leans on a ~$100 million tariff refund recognized in Q2 (worth ~470 basis points of that quarter's gross margin). Strip it out and the guide was effectively cut.
🔴 **EMEA is the swing region and it is exposed to the live oil shock** — management itself named higher fuel costs and Middle East demand as the drag in June; that driver has worsened since (the Hormuz blockade resumed in July 2026).
🟢 **Buyback with teeth** — 15% of shares retired in fiscal 2025, at least $300M more planned for fiscal 2026, funded from free cash flow.
🟢 **Operational promises kept** — the Calvin Klein product-organization fix landed on the promised quarter; inventory down 5%; deliveries on time.
🟢 **Forward order books positive** — Europe fall 2026 order books up, the second consecutive season of growth; a rare hard forward datapoint in apparel.
🟢 **Insider buying modestly positive** — open-market insiders bought 16,244 shares against 6,939 sold; small, but the direction is right at these prices.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The marketing vocabulary shifted from campaign-listing to *funnel economics* ("mid-funnel," "new consumer acquisition," "power segments") across fiscal 2025 — the company is measuring itself like a direct-to-consumer operator, which is where its margin future lives.
- Wholesale language cooled in steps: "benefited from earlier shipments" (Q1 2025) → "normalization" (Q2 2025) → "cautious partner positioning" (Q1 2026). Management never leads with this; it surfaces only in answers.
- Licensing is being quietly rebuilt as a growth lever — a new President of Global Licensing hired effective July 6, 2026, and the "go-forward license business is growing" — notable because royalty income is the highest-margin dollar in the company.
- The interim CFO's first solo call (June 2026) kept the same disclosure grain as her predecessor — continuity, not disruption.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is not a deteriorating franchise — it is a flat-revenue, trough-GAAP-earnings brand house that keeps its operational promises while external shocks (tariffs, then the Middle East conflict) keep eating the margin recovery it delivers. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **whether the ~$550 million of trailing free cash flow is durable through a European consumer downturn**, because the entire capital-return case (15% of the share count retired in a year, at least $300 million more coming) rests on it — and Europe is both the profit engine and the region now absorbing the oil-shock hit.

**Moat:** intangible-brand. Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger are genuinely global assets with pricing power in their hero categories, and the royalty stream monetizes them at near-pure margin. But the evidence caps the width: return on invested capital of 6%, return on equity of 9.4%, and a 0.3% net margin in the latest fiscal year are not wide-moat economics — they are a narrow moat rented out through a structurally thinner wholesale-heavy model. Gross margin at 57.5% is stable, not eroding, and the brand-heat indicators (order books, e-commerce growth, full-price sell-through) point sideways-to-better.

**Secular threat:** the relevant force is the retail channel shift — department-store wholesale, still a large share of the Americas business, is a structurally declining channel. PVH is migrating (e-commerce up mid-single digits, direct-to-consumer investment, licensing build-out) fast enough that this reads as a manageable drag on terminal value, not an impairment of it. The cheapness here is primarily a fear print on trough GAAP earnings and a live macro shock, not a structurally shrinking base — but it is also not a coiled spring: the multiple is low partly because the returns are low.

The call: wait for the wash-out, and be specific about it -- the entry trigger is either (a) a post-refund margin disappointment in the fall window that flushes the stock toward the low-to-mid $60s, where the adverse case is nearly paid for, or (b) hard evidence the European tax is lifting (de-escalation or a clean underlying-margin print), whichever comes first. Judged purely as a value case with no catalyst overlay, this is a four out of five -- an 18% discount to fair value with a compounding share count is genuinely attractive but not the deep, can't-lose discount a five requires on a 6% return-on-capital cyclical. Sized to the soft catalyst and the regime, we hold at a watchlist stance today.

interrogator_dossier:
# PVH Corp. (PVH) — Forensic Dossier
*Interrogator review of five consecutive earnings calls (June 2025 through June 2026, fiscal 2025 Q1 through fiscal 2026 Q1) cross-referenced against the screener financials. Price at review: $77.25 on the New York Stock Exchange, July 21, 2026.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has been remarkably consistent for five straight quarters: the "PVH+ plan" — lean into the brand strength of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, concentrate on hero categories (underwear and denim for Calvin, sweaters and outerwear for Tommy), amplify with celebrity-led marketing, and grind out cost savings. What changed across the arc is the *external* frame wrapped around that story:

- **June 2025 (Q1):** the first crack — "an increasingly tough environment," a leg down in North American consumer traffic, China weak, tariffs arriving. Full-year gross margin guidance cut from down ~100 basis points to down ~250, half of the extra pain from promotions.
- **August 2025 (Q2):** stabilization tone — beat on top and bottom line, guidance reaffirmed "despite tariff rates effectively doubling."
- **December 2025 (Q3):** confidence building — outlook narrowed to the high end; the Calvin Klein operational mess (late deliveries, weak going margins from standing up the New York global product organization) declared on track to be fixed for spring 2026. CFO Zac Coughlin's departure announced.
- **April 2026 (Q4/full year):** delivery — beat across revenue, operating profit and earnings per share; returned to revenue growth for the year as promised; a striking $560 million of buybacks retiring 15% of shares outstanding; fiscal 2026 guided flat-to-slightly-up with margins held at 8.8%.
- **June 2026 (Q1 fiscal 2026):** a new external shock — the prolonged Middle East conflict crushes the EMEA outlook (direct Middle East wholesale, Turkey knock-on, higher fuel costs suppressing European store traffic). Full-year revenue guidance cut to flat; earnings guidance held *only* because of a one-time ~$100 million tariff-refund benefit landing in Q2.

Two growth drivers were quietly re-weighted along the way: wholesale (early strength driven by shipment timing and the women's license take-back, now described with "cautious partner positioning") and Europe D2C (two strong quarters in early fiscal 2025, then muted). E-commerce and APAC were promoted from footnotes to lead proof points.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Returned to revenue growth" (fiscal 2025) | Revenue $8.95B vs $8.65B prior year, +3.4% reported | True, but reported growth got a currency assist; constant-currency was roughly flat. Five-year picture is a flat top line: $9.15B (fiscal 2022) to $8.95B (fiscal 2026) |
| "Delivered on all commitments across the P&L" | Guidance beaten 7 of 7 quarters (100% beat rate per the screener) | Corroborated — the beat cadence is real, though the bar is management's own guidance, which is set conservatively |
| Non-GAAP operating margin 8.8%, "11% excluding tariffs" | GAAP net income collapsed to $25M (EPS $0.53, down 95%) in fiscal 2026 | The widest GAAP/non-GAAP gap in the record. Roughly $790M of implied non-GAAP operating profit reconciles down to near-zero GAAP net income — tariffs, restructuring and one-time charges absorb almost everything. The adjusted story is much richer than the audited one |
| Strong cash generation funding buybacks | Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow $550M; $560M repurchased (15% of shares) in fiscal 2025 | Corroborated — buybacks are funded by genuine free cash flow, not leverage. The single strongest fact in the file |
| "Calvin Klein operational challenges fixed for spring 2026" | Q1 fiscal 2026: deliveries on time, going margins on plan, inventory down 5% | Delivered as promised, on the schedule set three quarters earlier — a genuine credibility win |
| Tariff mitigation "75% mitigated exiting this year" | Q3 fiscal 2025 gross margin down 210bp of which 110bp tariffs; Q2 fiscal 2026 to book a ~$100M refund | Mitigation is progressing but the refund is a one-time windfall, not mitigation. Watch whether fiscal 2027 margin holds without it |
| Balance sheet health | Net debt $3.63B including $1.94B of capitalized leases ($1.69B excluding leases) against $550M free cash flow; Altman-Z 2.2 (grey zone, not distress) | Manageable, not fortress. Roughly 3x free cash flow on the ex-lease measure |

The core divergence: management narrates brand momentum and beats; the audited financials show a company earning a 0.3% net margin and a 6% return on invested capital in its most recent fiscal year. The truth sits in between — trough GAAP earnings depressed by tariffs and one-offs, against real and improving cash generation (trailing-twelve-month diluted EPS $3.31, latest quarter up over 300% year on year).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive vocabulary creeping in.** Larsson's register barely moves quarter to quarter — the same "iconic brands, hero categories, full-funnel marketing" liturgy every call, which is itself information: no panic, but also little candor about demand. The tells:

- Q1 2025: "when the external factors get worse, it's time to sharpen our focus" — the pivot to controllables begins.
- Q2–Q4 2025: offense resumes ("beat our guidance on both the top and bottom line," "reaffirming... raising").
- Q1 2026: the "two opposing forces" framing — brand momentum versus the war — is the most defensive construction in the file, and the guidance cut it wraps is real.

Guidance specificity *increased* over time (basis-point-level tariff decompositions, region-by-region margin bridges), which typically signals a management team confident in its internal forecasting. The interim chief financial officer, Melissa Stone, has maintained that grain of disclosure.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High on execution, Medium on outlooks.** Every quarter in the record beat the guidance issued the quarter before, consistent with the screener's 7-for-7 beat rate. Two caveats: (1) there is a visible sandbagging pattern — guidance is set to be beaten, so each beat carries less signal than it appears; (2) the full-year outlook was cut twice in thirteen months on external shocks (promotions/tariffs in mid-2025, the Middle East conflict in mid-2026), so the beats coexist with a shrinking bar. Promises with hard deadlines — the spring 2026 Calvin Klein operational fix, the return to fiscal 2025 revenue growth, the 200-basis-point cost-savings program — were all delivered on schedule.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Gross margin recapture** (Boss, Kernan, Binetti, repeatedly): analysts kept probing when the ~250 basis points of fiscal-2025 margin give-up comes back. Management's answer — sequential improvement, spring 2026 going margins — was delivered, but the recapture is now hostage to tariffs and the promotional environment.
- **Macro versus execution attribution** (Boss, Q1 2025): how much of the weakness is self-inflicted? Management consistently attributes to macro; the Calvin operational mess was the one admitted own-goal.
- **Europe durability** (Roach, twice): what is the medium-term European growth algorithm? Management answers with order books (up low single digits), never with a demand algorithm — and Europe is precisely where the 2026 shock landed. The analysts were pulling on the right thread.
- **Wholesale caution** (Q1 2026): "cautious partner positioning" acknowledged — a soft leading indicator worth respecting.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The GAAP/non-GAAP chasm** — fiscal 2026 GAAP net income of $25M against a narrated 8.8% non-GAAP operating margin. The adjustments are individually defensible (tariffs, restructuring) but the cumulative gap is the largest in the company's recent record.
🔴 **CFO churn** — Coughlin out (announced December 2025), an interim chief financial officer through two earnings cycles and counting, with no permanent appointment as of July 2026.
🔴 **Earnings guidance held together by a one-timer** — the reaffirmed fiscal 2026 earnings guide leans on a ~$100 million tariff refund recognized in Q2 (worth ~470 basis points of that quarter's gross margin). Strip it out and the guide was effectively cut.
🔴 **EMEA is the swing region and it is exposed to the live oil shock** — management itself named higher fuel costs and Middle East demand as the drag in June; that driver has worsened since (the Hormuz blockade resumed in July 2026).
🟢 **Buyback with teeth** — 15% of shares retired in fiscal 2025, at least $300M more planned for fiscal 2026, funded from free cash flow.
🟢 **Operational promises kept** — the Calvin Klein product-organization fix landed on the promised quarter; inventory down 5%; deliveries on time.
🟢 **Forward order books positive** — Europe fall 2026 order books up, the second consecutive season of growth; a rare hard forward datapoint in apparel.
🟢 **Insider buying modestly positive** — open-market insiders bought 16,244 shares against 6,939 sold; small, but the direction is right at these prices.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The marketing vocabulary shifted from campaign-listing to *funnel economics* ("mid-funnel," "new consumer acquisition," "power segments") across fiscal 2025 — the company is measuring itself like a direct-to-consumer operator, which is where its margin future lives.
- Wholesale language cooled in steps: "benefited from earlier shipments" (Q1 2025) → "normalization" (Q2 2025) → "cautious partner positioning" (Q1 2026). Management never leads with this; it surfaces only in answers.
- Licensing is being quietly rebuilt as a growth lever — a new President of Global Licensing hired effective July 6, 2026, and the "go-forward license business is growing" — notable because royalty income is the highest-margin dollar in the company.
- The interim CFO's first solo call (June 2026) kept the same disclosure grain as her predecessor — continuity, not disruption.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** This is not a deteriorating franchise — it is a flat-revenue, trough-GAAP-earnings brand house that keeps its operational promises while external shocks (tariffs, then the Middle East conflict) keep eating the margin recovery it delivers. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **whether the ~$550 million of trailing free cash flow is durable through a European consumer downturn**, because the entire capital-return case (15% of the share count retired in a year, at least $300 million more coming) rests on it — and Europe is both the profit engine and the region now absorbing the oil-shock hit.

**Moat:** intangible-brand. Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger are genuinely global assets with pricing power in their hero categories, and the royalty stream monetizes them at near-pure margin. But the evidence caps the width: return on invested capital of 6%, return on equity of 9.4%, and a 0.3% net margin in the latest fiscal year are not wide-moat economics — they are a narrow moat rented out through a structurally thinner wholesale-heavy model. Gross margin at 57.5% is stable, not eroding, and the brand-heat indicators (order books, e-commerce growth, full-price sell-through) point sideways-to-better.

**Secular threat:** the relevant force is the retail channel shift — department-store wholesale, still a large share of the Americas business, is a structurally declining channel. PVH is migrating (e-commerce up mid-single digits, direct-to-consumer investment, licensing build-out) fast enough that this reads as a manageable drag on terminal value, not an impairment of it. The cheapness here is primarily a fear print on trough GAAP earnings and a live macro shock, not a structurally shrinking base — but it is also not a coiled spring: the multiple is low partly because the returns are low.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 4 | TRAJECTORY: STABLE | MOAT: NARROW | MOAT_TREND: STABLE | SECULAR_THREAT: manageable
